title: Finance 03 Â· Account balance window
objective: Compute previous_amount and running_net per account ordered by transaction_ts. Diagnose why the ordered account window requires an exchange and sort, and why a single hot account cannot be split across independent window tasks without changing semantics.
accepted_strategies: explicit ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW for running sum
keep all rows for one account co-located
anti_patterns: assume AQE can split one account's ordered window across tasks
solution:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import Window
w = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("transaction_ts")
result = (spark.table("silver.transactions")
    .withColumn("previous_amount", F.lag("amount").over(w))
    .withColumn("running_net", F.sum("amount").over(w.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow))))

counterexamples.name: Descending time reverses previous and running balances
counterexamples.source:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import Window
w = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy(F.col("transaction_ts").desc())
result = (spark.table("silver.transactions")
    .withColumn("previous_amount", F.lag("amount").over(w))
    .withColumn("running_net", F.sum("amount").over(w.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow))))

profile_comparison.invariant: Identical result rows; virtual timing and credits differ

aqe_comparison.invariant: Ordered hot account is never split; small buckets may coalesce
